abstract.p: Automatic evaluation of machine-generated texts, such as answers in open-domain question answering (Open-Domain QA), presents a complex challenge involving cost efficiency, hardware constraints, and high accuracy. Although various metrics exist for comparing machinegenerated answers with reference (gold standard) answers, ranging from lexical metrics (e.g., exact match) to semantic ones (e.g., cosine similarity) and using large language models (LLMs) as judges, none of these approaches achieves perfect performance in terms of accuracy or cost. To address this issue, we propose two approaches to enhance evaluation. First, we summarize long answers and use the shortened versions in the evaluation process, demonstrating that this adjustment significantly improves both lexical matching and semanticbased metrics evaluation results. Second, we introduce a multi-layered evaluation methodology that combines different metrics tailored to various scenarios. This combination of simple metrics delivers performance comparable to LLMs as judges but at lower costs. Moreover, our fused approach, which integrates both lexical and semantic metrics with LLMs through our formula, outperforms previous evaluation solutions.
